newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia eases work permit rules for foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia eases work permit rules for foreigners.

text.p: Malaysia has simplified immigration rules for foreigners in a bid to attract more skilled workers, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Monday.

"I would like to announce that the procedure for expatriate work-permit approval has been simplified," Anwar said at the launch of Malaysian Life Reinsurance Group Bhd, the country's first life reinsurance firm.
From May 1, the authorities and agencies responsible for certain sectors of the economy have been given the responsibility for approving work permits, he said.
"The immigration department will endorse the approvals and issue the relevant documents to the applicants," Anwar said.
He said the new arrangement would speed up the issue of work permits. According to many expatriates, permits can take up to 10 months or more to be issued, depending on the sector.
Malaysia has been trying to attract more skilled foreigners as part of its efforts to make Kuala Lumpur a regional financial and technological centre.
It recently proposed a Multimedia Super Corridor, a 15 km by 50 km (31 mile by 31 mile) zone in and around Kuala Lumpur to promote investment in high technology industries.
